# Clocks

Performance counters, system time and tick counts.

<h2 id="query-performance-counter"><code>QueryPerformanceCounter</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func QueryPerformanceCounter(count: *var int64) -> int32
```

Reads the monotonic performance counter.
Writes the current count and returns nonzero. It cannot fail on any system this package supports, and the
count is guaranteed not to go backwards — unlike the wall clock, which can. The unit is whatever
QueryPerformanceFrequency reports and is not seconds.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/profileapi/nf-profileapi-queryperformancecounter](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/profileapi/nf-profileapi-queryperformancecounter)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Clock.rux#L34)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type         | Description                          |
| ------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `count` | `*var int64` | receives the counter's current value |

**Returns**: non-zero on success

<h2 id="query-performance-frequency"><code>QueryPerformanceFrequency</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func QueryPerformanceFrequency(frequency: *var int64) -> int32
```

Reads how many performance-counter ticks make one second.
Fixed while the system runs, so a caller reads it once rather than per measurement.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/profileapi/nf-profileapi-queryperformancefrequency](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/profileapi/nf-profileapi-queryperformancefrequency)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Clock.rux#L42)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type         | Description                                                  |
| ----------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `frequency` | `*var int64` | receives the counter's fixed frequency, in counts per second |

**Returns**: non-zero on success

<h2 id="get-system-time-precise-as-file-time"><code>GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime(time: *var FileTime)
```

Reads the current wall-clock time at the highest resolution the system offers.
Writes 100-nanosecond intervals since January 1, 1601 UTC. The plain GetSystemTimeAsFileTime is cheaper and
coarser, advancing only at the scheduler's tick.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getsystemtimepreciseasfiletime](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getsystemtimepreciseasfiletime)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Clock.rux#L50)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type            | Description          |
| ------ | --------------- | -------------------- |
| `time` | `*var FileTime` | receives the reading |

<h2 id="get-tick-count64"><code>GetTickCount64</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func GetTickCount64() -> uint64
```

Retrieves the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the system was started.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-gettickcount64](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-gettickcount64)
